title: Add five deterministic checks for a decision question
description: Add question_shape, diagram_present, diagram_size, diagram_parses and diagram_labels as deterministic harness checks, each proved both ways, per the design in opum-doc docs/reference/operator-questions-skill-design.md at opum-doc origin/main 1312f0c, section Changes this needs in plain-english-styles item 5.

acceptanceCriteria.text: question_shape, diagram_present, diagram_size, diagram_parses and diagram_labels each exist in the checks registry
Each of the five is proved both ways: it passes on a conforming reply and fails on a non-conforming one
diagram_size enforces the level node cap and diagram_labels rejects Beginner banned terms in node labels
diagram_parses uses the Mermaid parser and rejects a source it cannot parse

finalSummary:
Adds the five deterministic checks: question_shape, diagram_present, diagram_size, diagram_parses and diagram_labels, each proved both ways. They fire only where a case names them in caseDef.checks; none is in a styles defaultChecks, so ordinary replies are not scored against a shape they do not have.

question_shape: the question line, A, B, a recommendation, C and the three trade-off axes (cost, quality, speed), matched as concepts so Beginner everyday words (safer, costs nothing, faster) count. diagram_present: exactly one mermaid fence. diagram_size: node count against the level cap (Beginner 5, Intermediate 8, Advanced 12). diagram_labels: no banned term inside a node label. diagram_parses: Mermaid own parser.

diagram_parses needed a decision: mermaid.parse is asynchronous and needs a DOM (its parse path runs DOMPurify), while scoreDeterministic is synchronous. It runs in a child process, harness/src/mermaid-parse.mjs, source on stdin, exit 0 or 1, called through execFileSync. Cost noted for review: mermaid and jsdom are new harness dependencies - node_modules grows by about 128 MB (gitignored; the committed change is package.json plus package-lock.json), and one parse costs about 0.35 s.

Proved both ways, and each check mutated to prove its tests reject: tradeoffs forced false, diagram_present relaxed to n >= 1, the node cap ignored, the parse result ignored, the label hits ignored - each reddened exactly its own test, 1 failed / 257 passed, then restored and re-verified.

Gates: npm --prefix harness test 258 pass / 0 fail (was 252); node src/cli.mjs audit exit 0, all 12 checks agree; claude plugin test 21/21; claude plugin validate exit 0.

Note added after review. diagram_parses certifies the BROWSER renderer only: it runs Mermaid own parser, the library the plugin vendors as renderer/vendor/mermaid.min.js, so it speaks for what the browser view draws. The terminal path uses beautiful-mermaid (renderer/render.mjs), a DIFFERENT parser, so a diagram that passes here is not thereby certified to draw as terminal art. Follow-up: PES-8 can add a case for a diagram one accepts and the other rejects, if one is found. Also pinned the harness to the exact vendored versions - mermaid 11.17.2 and jsdom 30.1.2, both without a caret - and added a test asserting the harness resolved mermaid equals the version in renderer/licenses/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md, so the two cannot drift silently; mermaid 11.17.2 parse API needed no change.
